title: CRASH-022: user sort comparator frees live bucket uaf (use-after-free)
live_proof: measured, not asserted: our native ASan build of the pinned 5.0.0 tarball (p12, gcc 15.2.0, libasan from gcc 15, 2026-10-27) reports ASAN:heap-use-after-free at ext/standard/array.c:546 in array_user_compare when trigger.php runs; the corpus records the fix as php-src 18a0d46a1b44, which postdates the release, and names the defect at ext/standard/array.c:546
fidelity: the corpus's own trigger script, run through the real interpreter (PHP's cli SAPI, ext/standard only, the port's 145 translation units) rather than reduced to a C model. What it does NOT establish is which arm ought to catch it. The pristine build completes it natively, so an arm that completes it saw nothing.
fault_sites_why: ASan's access stack in our native run (results-ours-asan-default.json, sha256 045e3366bfc5) has array_user_compare at ext/standard/array.c:546 as its first frame inside PHP's tree (frame #0); the stack's remaining frames are the interpreter's dispatch and are not sites

virtual-malloc.oracle: the case on the virtual profile with the nested layer present but returning every freed block's loan, so only musl mallocng revokes, per BLOCK, when PHP's cache hands a block back to free(): a fault at the ASan site, or the trigger ends and this arm did not see it (tools/arms.json php-real-block)
virtual-malloc.verdict_note: cause=25 pc=0x3f9d4beb20 in array_user_compare; by function: array_user_compare at ext/standard/array.c:546 is the function this case declares (fault_sites, ASan frame #0 of our native run), at ASan's own line

virtual-nested-pools.oracle: the same image with the nested allocator layer retiring the payload at EVERY _efree, cache-absorbed or not, and re-deriving it under a fresh node when the cache hands the block to its next tenant: a fault at the ASan site, or the trigger ends and this arm did not see it (php-real-object)
virtual-nested-pools.verdict_note: cause=25 pc=0x3f864beb20 in array_user_compare; by function: array_user_compare at ext/standard/array.c:546 is the function this case declares (fault_sites, ASan frame #0 of our native run), at ASan's own line

virtual-nested-exact.oracle: virtual-nested-pools with each payload bounded to the caller's request instead of REAL_SIZE(n): the arm that can see a defect inside PHP's own rounding slack (php-real-exact)
virtual-nested-exact.verdict_note: cause=25 pc=0x3fa0cbeb20 in array_user_compare; by function: array_user_compare at ext/standard/array.c:546 is the function this case declares (fault_sites, ASan frame #0 of our native run), at ASan's own line

cheribsd-revocation.oracle: the same trigger on stock CheriBSD purecap -- no nested layer at all, the real interpreter cross-built by ports/php/cheribsd/build.sh -- in the boot at the platform default (security.cheri.runtime_revocation_default=1, every_free=0): a SIGPROT at the ASan site with the bounds-malloc control faulting in the same boot, the same binary run with revocation off as the pair that attributes the fault, or the trigger ends and this arm did not see it (tools/arms.json cheribsd-default)
cheribsd-revocation.verdict_note: neither a capability fault nor a clean exit -- ALLOCATOR-ABORT: CheriBSD's allocator aborted, the signature its own double-free check produces (ports/php/cheribsd/results/20261029-allocator-probe). Not a capability fault; with revocation off this case exited 0; NOT-REISSUED: no capability fault at the platform default, but the eager configuration (runtime_revocation_every_free_default=1) faults on this case, so the stale pointer IS followed. The eager fault lands inside the script body, which is what tells a revoked object apart from the allocator's cache being drained back to libc at shutdown. Context, not a verdict: every-free also faults on accesses nothing is meant to catch

status: built 2026-10-27 from the corpus and our native oracle; what has run is in this record's arms (verdict, verdict_from) and under results/
note: population: asan-blind -- ASan reports it only with PHP's allocator patched (cache off, no 8-byte rounding); with zend_alloc.c as shipped the run reads OK. That is the selection, by measurement; which mechanism hides it, and which arm sees it, is what the arms record. Collected by the corpus as carried-from-4.0.2 (historical-known, confidence medium).
